items.title: Detectable Full / reopen trigger: Apply material-decision contract when Sizing-Gate is Full, operator-directed Full-depth questioning is already underway, or reopen/continuation after declared-ready / Rule 6 confirmation. Out of scope unless reopened into Full: Light, Add-scope short path, Update/delta that stays delta.

One material-decision inventory as depth bound: Material-decision inventory is the depth-bound for when questioning may stop (deliverable, material required decisions with resolution conditions, approved constraints, accepted deferrals, completion conditions). Seven-key Full Path Output remains output-shape narratives. Rule 4 completeness reads the inventory; Rule 7 answers-map still requires non-deferred caller-required keys. Do not ship a competing second required-field list.

Authorship, confirm, freeze: Agent may draft inventory; operator must explicitly confirm before depth-gate completion pressure. Mark operator-named vs agent-derived provenance; refuse inventing approved constraints/deferrals. After confirm, mutation uses operator-visible diff + re-confirm; silent thin-then-widen refuse.

Phase-relative sufficiency + follow-up cites: Each material decision carries a resolution condition. New asks must (a) cite outstanding material requirement within resolution condition, (b) revisit accepted deferral with boundary change, or (c) operator-raised gap after declared-ready with inventory amendment + re-confirm. Routine clarification inside an existing condition needs no extra approval.

Deferrals vs handoff: Distinguish resolved / deferred-for-this-phase / still-blocking. Deferral records unresolved decision, why non-blocking, and later trigger — not a fabricated answers-map value. Required values remain enforced where caller needs them now.

Persistence on continuation: Carry target deliverable, inventory dispositions, and accepted boundary changes in working artifact / answers handoff and reload on continuation. Do not reconstruct a fresh maximal inventory on resume.

Question Areas land + phase-scope: Phase-scope Implementation details Question Area so it cannot keep ordering unbounded detail asks after inventory confirm. Reconcile setup MUST vs strategy SHOULD on little-ambiguity to inventory sufficiency strength. Land in setup Phase 3, strategies/interview, make-spec templates.

Completion evidence via Confirmation Gate: Extend Rule 6 Confirmation Gate: summary lists inventory as decided / deferred-with-permit / out-of-phase; require explicit affirm; refuse treating artifact write success alone as completion. Extend re-ask-those-specific-questions bound to post-gate reopen (item 4c).

Acceptance honesty + evaluator fixture: Pack prose + presence tests at land sites. At least one pure evaluator/fixture for inventory sufficiency + follow-up cite rules covering finite inventory confirm, focused follow-up, deferral persistence, no silent widen, inventory-supported completion. Do not claim behavioral closure from toContain alone.

x-directive/disposition.reason: Expressly deferred pure evaluator/fixture after product PR #5359 (Tracking #5351); pack prose + presence tests shipped; evaluator remainder stays deferred.

CHANGELOG Unreleased.

mechanism-shaped: true
design-critique: warranted, because Full/brownfield interview completion is gated only by open-ended "no material ambiguity remains" while the required-field handoff is SHOULD and setup Phase 3 / strategy transition use broad subject areas, so the agent can redefine the prerequisite set after every answer and never reach a bounded deliverable.

yolo-standing: yes
dest: C:\Repos\deft\directive\.deft-scratch\worktrees\arc-5351
origin-ref: origin/master
dispatch-sha: 3456c6712614e352c5559b3c29caf9cbce26b5cf

spend: N≥3
spend-ask: asked
spend-recommend: N≥3
spend-why: Prefer-A drafted from the issue's requested remedy (adaptive but bounded material-decision contract across interview Rule 4, setup Phase 3, and strategy transition). Solution space is open on where the contract lives and how materiality/deferrals are encoded; blast spans interview + setup + strategy pack sources. Operator cue "arc using recommended n 5351" takes closed spend-recommend with spend-ask: asked.
Dual-stop cap: 6 posts
dual-stop-reserved: first post-lean pain-audit of asserted coverage is in-cap via Dual-stop reserved slot; raise only after that reserved seat is spent

pain: P1, P2, P3

- P1. Unbounded depth: Interview Rule 4 MUST keep asking until no material ambiguity remains, but the required-field list that defines sufficient specificity is only SHOULD, so embedded Full interviews can invent new mandatory technical decisions indefinitely after each answer.
- P2. Broad completion criteria: setup Phase 3 / strategy transition name subject areas and "comprehensive enough to implement" / "all major decisions and edge cases" without a phase-specific materiality inventory (deliverable, required decisions, approved constraints, accepted deferrals, completion conditions), so the boundary can move without an explicit contract change.
- P3. Silent prerequisite growth: a newly discovered question need not map to an outstanding material requirement for the current deliverable; derived implementation details (payload fields, SQL sequences, UI copy) can silently widen the phase and reopen after a declared-ready state.

related: #4377 #1176 #1709 interview Rule 4 setup Phase 3 strategies/interview.md consumer feedback 2026-10-04

## Prefer-A draft (charter target; not yet Bound)

1. **Bounded material-decision contract (P1/P2).** For Full/brownfield interviews, require a named inventory before depth-gate completion: target deliverable, material required decisions, approved constraints, accepted deferrals, and completion conditions. Raise the required-field handoff from SHOULD to a MUST for embedded Full paths that today rely on subjective completeness.
2. **Follow-up must cite material requirement (P3).** A newly discovered question MUST name which outstanding material requirement it resolves (or which accepted deferral it revisits with operator-visible boundary change). Derived implementation details outside the current phase MUST NOT silently become phase prerequisites.
3. **Preserve adaptivity.** Keep answer-dependent branching and legitimate clarifications. Do not replace with a universal question cap, a complete up-front questionnaire, or extra approval for routine in-bound choices.
4. **Completion evidence.** Completion is supported by the decision inventory; artifact validity alone cannot establish it. Named source/model/performance deferrals may remain open when the contract permits them without blocking the bounded requirements phase.
5. **Land sites.** Fix canonical pack sources (interview skill Rule 4 / embedded vs delegation, setup Phase 3 completion, strategies/interview transition criteria) and regenerate dependent instructions.
6. **Non-goals / distinct.** Distinct from #4377 transport/form and #1176 implementation-plan placeholder validation. No adoption-blocker classification asserted. No universal question cap.

## Gate stamp

Fresh no-ingest yolo Stop 1 on #5351. Operator cue "arc using recommended n 5351" → arc-mode no-ingest (host default), yolo standing on, Dual-stop spend taken from closed spend-recommend N≥3 with spend-ask: asked. Prefer-A drafted from issue remediations. Charter is open critique of that Prefer-A. Ingest remains a later separate verb.

audit-targets: none

Round 1 open critique of Prefer-A at Stop 1, comment 5986231390. Input ceiling: 5986241123. Verified by `git show 3456c6712614e352c5559b3c29caf9cbce26b5cf:<path>` and bounded REST reads of the issue body, Stop 1, and panel deposit. No sibling posts read. These are source-contract findings, not a reproduced model-behavior measurement or a pain audit.

Existing mechanisms first: [Interview Rules 4-7 and Invocation Contract](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/3456c6712614e352c5559b3c29caf9cbce26b5cf/content/skills/deft-directive-interview/SKILL.md) already provide caller-defined required inputs, explicit confirmation, a structured answers map, optional keys, and mandatory required-field definitions for delegation. Embedded mode already permits field requirements inline without a formal contract object. [Setup Phase 3](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/3456c6712614e352c5559b3c29caf9cbce26b5cf/content/skills/deft-directive-setup/SKILL.md#L695) distinguishes Add scope, delta update, replacement, and Starting new; brownfield alone does not select Full. [Interview strategy](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/3456c6712614e352c5559b3c29caf9cbce26b5cf/content/strategies/interview.md#L275) already preserves questions/answers in the working document, includes deferred implementation decisions in Open Questions (lines 420-421), and distinguishes nonblocking questions at the PRD transition (lines 432-437). Prefer-A should tighten these mechanisms rather than create a second interview or approval system.

### 1. blocks-the-design — Requirement citation does not bound decision depth

Evidence: Prefer-A items 1-2 require an inventory before completion and a citation to an outstanding material requirement. They do not say when that requirement has sufficient evidence to stop, or how a newly discovered material decision enters the inventory. At the pin, Rule 4 still requires clarification when an answer introduces ambiguity; setup lines 798-812 and strategy lines 286-300 include implementation details and broad completeness obligations.

Concrete failure: an inventory row called "report reliability" can remain outstanding while the agent asks about retries, leases, clocks, transaction boundaries, and every SQL sequence. Every question truthfully cites that same row. Nothing need silently widen the named phase, yet the original endless-depth failure survives. Conversely, a genuinely new material concern revealed by an answer might fit neither an outstanding row nor an accepted deferral, so a literal reading of item 2 can suppress necessary discovery.

Disposition consequence: Prefer-A cannot bind as written. The bounded object needs a phase-relative sufficiency rule established before depth questioning, with incremental population allowed: a decision is mandatory now when leaving it unresolved would change the current deliverable's required behavior, constraints, acceptance, or feasibility; a choice among implementations already satisfying those conditions need not block this phase. Existing rows need a stated resolution condition, not only a name. Newly discovered material decisions need a visible inventory amendment and reason; routine clarification within an existing condition needs no extra approval. A new phase prerequisite is distinguishable from a new answer to the same prerequisite. This supplies the missing limit without freezing the questionnaire or imposing a question count.

### 2. sharpens-framing — Permitted deferral must reconcile with the existing handoff

Evidence: Prefer-A item 4 allows named deferrals when the contract permits them. Rule 7 requires a value for every required key; Rule 4 requires sufficient specificity before generation. Strategy already has Open Questions for implementation deferrals and a nonblocking-open-question distinction.

Concrete failure: a performance target is marked deferred in the inventory, but its required answers-map key remains absent. The handoff can then reopen questioning, or fill in an invented target to satisfy required-key completeness. The inventory and existing completion rules disagree even though the draft says the deferral is allowed.

Disposition consequence: the direction can bind with an explicit reconciliation: resolved, legitimately deferred for this phase, and still blocking are different outcomes. A deferral carries the unresolved decision, why it does not block this deliverable, and the later trigger for resolving it; it is not a fabricated answer. Its representation belongs in the existing handoff/working artifact, with required values still enforced where the caller actually needs them now. No universal exemption from required fields and no duplicate approval gate are needed.

### 3. sharpens-framing — Name the phase and preserve its boundary on continuation

Evidence: the issue's observation includes a continuation session. Prefer-A names a target deliverable but no persisted location or resume rule. Strategy line 284 already requires appending questions and answers to the working document. Setup lines 716-722 distinguish brownfield routes, while the interview skill's Output Targets delegate artifact authority to the caller.

Concrete failure: a resumed agent sees completed answers but reconstructs a fresh mandatory inventory from broad "comprehensive enough to implement" guidance. Or a requirements-phase deferral is treated as permission to leave the same decision unresolved in a later implementation-planning phase. Both lose the phase boundary despite a correct first session.

Disposition consequence: scope the obligation to the actual Full interview phase, including operator-requested Full brownfield work, rather than all brownfield routing. Carry the target deliverable, inventory dispositions, and accepted boundary changes in the caller's existing working artifact/answers handoff and reload them on continuation. Requirements completion and implementation readiness stay separate claims. This is a persistence clarification, not a new artifact family.

Authority/injection lens: this inventory becomes a source of completion authority. Repository documents and imported issue text can supply evidence or candidate questions; they cannot silently become operator-approved constraints, deferrals, or phase amendments. Existing external-content defenses remain applicable. There is no need to introduce a swarm allocation mechanism for this change.

Road not taken: a frozen upfront checklist would make missing entries easy to detect, but would mishandle genuinely answer-dependent risks. A universal turn cap would bound cost without establishing completeness. The stronger version of Prefer-A is an evolving inventory with stable phase-relative resolution conditions. A concrete condition that rejects the reliability/lease/clock chain while admitting a newly discovered consequential ambiguity would remove finding 1.

Plain take: the draft chooses the right direction, but a named list and a requirement citation alone can still support an endless interview. It needs a clear rule for when a decision is settled, how genuinely new decisions enter, and how deferrals and that boundary survive handoff and continuation.

round: 1
critic-role: fresh
target: #5351
audit-targets: none
charter: open critique of Prefer-A draft on Stop 1 (5986231390)
dispatch-sha: 3456c6712614e352c5559b3c29caf9cbce26b5cf
input-ceiling: 5986241123
seat: grok

## Re-verify (pin 3456c671)

Pin-read via `git show 3456c6712614e352c5559b3c29caf9cbce26b5cf:` confirms Stop 1 anchors:

- Interview Rule 4 Depth Gate: MUST keep asking until no material ambiguity remains; required-field handoff is SHOULD (`~`) only.
- Embedded Mode: no formal contract object; caller embeds field requirements in its own skill. Delegation Mode already MUST-provides required fields / question defs / optional fields for completeness.
- Setup Phase 3 **Completion**: `Continue until little ambiguity remains` + `Spec must be comprehensive enough to implement` — no named inventory.
- Setup + strategy **Question Areas**: both mark `Implementation details (architecture, patterns, libraries)` as MUST (`!`).
- Strategy **Transition Criteria (interview complete)**: all major decisions / edge cases / approved tradeoffs / little ambiguity — no phase-specific materiality inventory.
- PRD section separately forbids packing implementation details into the PRD artifact (`⊗ Include implementation details or architecture`) while the shared interview Question Areas still MUST-cover them — authority split already exists for artifact shape, not for ask-set bounding.

Target-digest on Stop 1 (`sha256:becae779…6edc`) does not match live REST `.body` SHA-256 `sha256:e10f38550461b1786c7908ca5173448a0f46b7da0a6ede63162f3eb332ff28aa` (5625 UTF-8 bytes) at critic time. Treat as parent hygiene; Prefer-A prose is still the charter target.

## Inventory (existing mechanisms before new ones)

| Mechanism | What it already does | Gap vs Prefer-A / P1–P3 |
|---|---|---|
| Delegation Mode required-fields | Depth-gate completeness from a formal field list | Embedded Full/setup Phase 3 does not use it |
| Embedded Mode caller-owned fields | Phase 1/2 embed concrete questions in setup skill | Phase 3 Full has subject areas, not a finite decision inventory |
| Rule 6 / Post-Interview Confirmation Gate | Confirms captured values before write | End-of-ask confirmation; does not freeze the ask-set / material inventory up front |
| Operator scope-limit (#4545) | Closed-lexicon hard ceiling on seeded brief surfaces | Product-scope ceiling after/beside interview; not a material-decision inventory for adaptive Q&A |
| `ambiguity_attestation` / plan.acceptance | Post-write AC stamp fields | Explicitly not emitted from setup interview; not completion evidence for the ask phase |
| #4377 up-front form/TUI | Transport/batching of questions | Prefer-A correctly distinct (preserves adaptive one-at-a-time) |
| #1176 verify:plan / no-placeholders | Plan completeness after planning artifacts | Prefer-A correctly distinct (interview boundary, not placeholder validation) |

Prefer-A's named inventory is the right *kind* of control. The open critique is whether the draft is specific enough to relieve P1–P3 without fighting other MUST pressure still in the pack.

## Findings

### F1. Inventory authorship, confirm, and freeze are unspecified
**class:** `blocks-the-design`

**evidence:** Prefer-A item 1 requires a named inventory (deliverable, material decisions, constraints, deferrals, completion conditions) and raises Rule 4's required-field handoff to MUST for embedded Full, but does not say who authors the inventory, when the operator confirms it, or when it freezes. Rule 6 / Post-Interview Confirmation Gate only confirms captured *answers* after the depth gate claims satisfaction. Item 2 covers follow-up cites / deferral revisits, not first publication of an agent-maximal inventory.

**failure mode:** Agent publishes a maximal inventory that restates Question Areas (including every implementation detail) as "material," then never closes; or publishes a thin inventory and later widens it without an operator-visible boundary change because mutability of the inventory itself is unnamed. P1/P2 recur inside the new artifact.

**disposition consequence:** Prefer-A cannot bind as written. Bound must add: (a) proposer (agent-draft vs operator-seed), (b) explicit operator confirm of the inventory *before* depth-gate completion pressure applies, (c) freeze rule — inventory mutation uses the same operator-visible boundary-change path item 2 already sketches for deferral revisits.

### F2. Question Areas still MUST-cover Implementation details; land sites omit them
**class:** `blocks-the-design`

**evidence:** Prefer-A land sites name Rule 4 / embedded-vs-delegation, setup Phase 3 completion, and strategies/interview transition criteria. They omit shared **Question Areas** in both `content/skills/deft-directive-setup/SKILL.md` (Phase 3 Interview Process) and `content/strategies/interview.md`, where `Implementation details` is `!`. Issue session notes and P3 describe exactly that MUST pressure (payload fields, SQL sequences, UI copy) after a declared-ready state.

**failure mode:** Bound raises completion to an inventory while the same pack still orders agents to cover implementation details as a mandatory question area. Agents obey the stronger local MUST and silently re-widen after "complete," recreating P3.

**disposition consequence:** Prefer-A cannot bind without adding Question Areas to land sites and demoting or phase-scoping `Implementation details` (and possibly unbounded edge-case expansion) for the bounded requirements / planning deliverable phase. Artifact-side `⊗` in the PRD section is not enough — that forbids packing details into PRD text, not asking them forever.

### F3. "Raise SHOULD→MUST" without a callee-published list leaves Rule 4 pointing at air
**class:** `sharpens-framing`

**evidence:** Rule 4 today: completeness = calling skill's required inputs at sufficient specificity; specificity list is SHOULD via handoff. Embedded Mode says no formal contract object — caller embeds requirements in its own SKILL. Prefer-A item 1 raises the handoff to MUST for embedded Full, and separately requires a named inventory, but does not say the inventory *is* that required-field list (or how it differs from Delegation Mode's formal object).

**failure mode:** Implementers raise the RFC keyword on Rule 4 while setup Phase 3 still only has prose Completion bullets; the MUST has no on-disk list to enforce against. Dual vocabulary ("material-decision contract" vs "required fields") forks without a mapping.

**disposition consequence:** Lean can bind after stating: the named inventory *is* the embedded Full required-field handoff surface (reuse Delegation Mode semantics without forcing a sub-skill invoke), published in setup/strategy land sites, not a parallel undefined object.

### F4. Scope of Prefer-A across Light / Add-scope / continuation is fuzzy
**class:** `sharpens-framing`

**evidence:** Charter and Prefer-A say Full/brownfield. Shared Interview Rules + Completion/Transition Criteria also gate Light. Setup brownfield **Add-scope** skips the full interview after an explicit product/slice description. Issue context includes a continuation session after an approved artifact batch and a reopen after declared-ready — the P3 shape.

## Bind map (Prefer-A Bound)

Bind Approach A — adaptive but bounded material-decision contract for the detectable Full interview path and for reopen/continuation after a declared-ready or confirmed summary. ### 1. Detectable trigger (Claude F1)

- Sizing-Gate outcome is **Full** (greenfield Full, or brownfield Replace that reached Sizing after confirmed scrap), or
- an operator-directed interview that has already entered Full-depth questioning (including a brownfield session that skipped Chaining but is already behaving as Full — treat as conformance debt; still apply the bound rather than invent a "Full/brownfield" compound state), or
- **reopen / continuation** after a declared-ready state or after Rule 6 confirmation (Grok F4).

Out of scope unless reopened into Full depth: Light sizing; Add-scope short path; Update/delta interview that stays delta.

### 2. One inventory, not a second list (Claude F2 / Grok F3)

The named material-decision inventory **is** the embedded Full required-field handoff surface (reuse Delegation Mode semantics without forcing a sub-skill invoke). Relation to the existing seven-key Full Path Output set (`ProblemStatement` … `Overview` at interview Full Path Output / setup Phase 3):
- Seven-key set = **output-shape** narratives that must be filled for Full artifact write.
- Material-decision inventory = **depth-bound** for when questioning may stop (deliverable, material required decisions with resolution conditions, approved constraints, accepted deferrals, completion conditions).
- Rule 4 completeness reads the inventory for ask-set sufficiency; Rule 7 answers-map completeness still requires values for every caller-required key that is **not** legitimately deferred for this phase.
- Do not ship a competing undefined second required-field list. Do not reframe the existing seven-key MUST as "only SHOULD."

### 3. Authorship, confirm, freeze (Grok F1 / Claude F4)

- Proposer: agent may **draft** the inventory from conversation + pack defaults.
- Confirm: operator must explicitly confirm the inventory **before** depth-gate completion pressure applies (and before treating the ask-set as closed).
- Provenance: each inventory member is marked operator-named vs agent-derived; ⊗ invent approved constraints or accepted deferrals as if operator-approved (match file_scope / #4545 polarity).
- Freeze: after confirm, inventory mutation uses the same operator-visible boundary-change path as item 4 (diff + re-confirm). Silent agent-maximal or silent thin-then-widen inventories are refuse.

### 4. Phase-relative sufficiency + follow-up cites (Codex F1 / Claude F3)

Before depth questioning under a confirmed inventory:
- Each material required decision carries a **resolution condition** (what evidence settles it for this deliverable), not only a name.
- A decision is mandatory for this phase when leaving it unresolved would change the current deliverable's required behavior, constraints, acceptance, or feasibility.
- A choice among implementations that already satisfy those conditions need not block this phase.

Newly discovered questions:
- (a) cite an outstanding material requirement and stay within its resolution condition, or
- (b) revisit an accepted deferral with operator-visible boundary change, or
- (c) **operator-raised gap / inventory defect** after declared-ready: operator-visible inventory amendment (diff) then re-confirm — covers the audited UI-behavior recovery that (a)/(b) alone would forbid.

Routine clarification inside an existing resolution condition needs no extra approval. Distinguishing a new phase prerequisite from a new answer to the same prerequisite is required.

### 5. Deferrals vs handoff (Codex F2)

Resolved / legitimately deferred-for-this-phase / still-blocking are distinct outcomes. A deferral records: the unresolved decision, why it does not block this deliverable, and the later trigger. It is not a fabricated answers-map value. Represent deferrals in the existing handoff / working artifact. Required values remain enforced where the caller needs them now. No universal exemption from required fields.

### 6. Persistence on continuation (Codex F3)

Carry target deliverable, inventory dispositions, and accepted boundary changes in the caller's existing working artifact / answers handoff and reload them on continuation. Requirements-phase completion and implementation readiness stay separate claims. Do not reconstruct a fresh maximal inventory from "comprehensive enough to implement" on resume.

- Artifact-side ⊗ packing implementation details into PRD text remains; that alone does not bound the ask-set.

### 8. Completion evidence via Confirmation Gate (Grok F5 / Claude F7)

v1 completion evidence extends Rule 6 Confirmation Gate: summary lists inventory items as decided / deferred-with-permit / out-of-phase; require explicit affirm; ⊗ treat artifact write success alone as completion. Defer a new `verify:*` verb unless a later pain forces it (#1176 stays distinct).
